description:
Found while writing examples/codecs.exs (defk-9p6.19): `alloc(u8, n)` zero-fills the buffer with one memset (defk_own in priv/defk_runtime.h), so an 85 MB allocation holds the scheduler for ~5 ms before the kernel's first loop runs; the tick gap during a 64 MB base64 encode was 4.6-6.6 ms, against the 2.3 ms a yielding loop keeps. Elixir mode defines alloc as a zeroed binary, so the zeroing must stay semantically; it does not have to be one memset.

Options: (a) zero in strips of a few MB with a safepoint between them (a loop in the generated C around the memset, charged to the budget like any loop; the frame must spill the partially-zeroed state: the alloc's slot index and the offset); (b) allocate without zeroing when the compiler can prove every element is written before any read (common: `for i <- ...: out[i] = ...` over the full range), keeping the memset otherwise; (c) both. Measure (b)'s win on scale/image_resize/codecs (memset is a full extra pass over the output).

Done when: an 85 MB alloc shows a worst tick gap in line with a yielding loop (bench/tick_gap.exs style test), and either (b) is implemented with a test on the generated C or recorded as a follow-up with numbers.
title: A large alloc/2 zero-fills without a safepoint: 85 MB costs a 5 ms scheduler gap
